Rashi on Niddah 20a:10:1.english: And all of them - The five types of blood.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:10:2.english: A white cloth - The colors of the blood are discernible on it.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:10:3.hebrew: ושחור - דם שחור, נבדקה מראיתו אם שחור היא כחרת או דיהה מכן, על גבי בגד אדום:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:10:3.english: And black - [Regarding] black blood, its appearance is examined—whether it is as black as ḥeret or lighter than it—upon a red garment.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:12:1.english: All of them - The [types of] blood.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:12:2.hebrew: עמוק מכן - מאותו שיעור השנוי במתניתין לכל אחד, אי הוה סומק טפי, טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:12:2.english: Deeper than this - [Deeper] than that standard taught in the mishna for each one; if it was redder, it is ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:12:3.hebrew: דיהה מכן טהור כשחור - ואע"פ דלא תנן במתניתין דיהה מכן טהור אלא גבי שחור, הוא הדין לכולהו:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:12:3.english: Lighter than this is pure, like black - And even though we did not learn in the mishna "lighter than this is pure" except regarding black, the same applies to all of them.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:13:1.english: Even lighter than this should be impure - For this was red, and through an affliction it became black.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:13:2.english: It teaches us - That it is not the way of red blood that turns black through deterioration to be faint.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:14:1.english: Lighter than light - That it has deviated excessively from its appearance.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:16:1.hebrew: עמוק מכן טהור - אם מאותו מראה הוא, אבל אם האדים הרבה עד שבא לכלל אחד משאר המראות של מעלה הימנו, הרי בא לחדא מהנך דמתני':
Rashi on Niddah 20a:16:1.english: Deeper than that is pure - [This applies only] if it is of that [same] appearance; but if it reddened significantly, until it reached the category of one of the other appearances that are above it, it has indeed entered [the status of] one of those [appearances taught] in the mishna.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:16:2.english: Which [one] was it to him? - Blood resembling diluted wine.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:18:1.english: Like the bottom - The bottom leaf.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:19:1.english: Three rows - They were [rows] of leaves, one above the other.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:1:1.hebrew: בקילור - אנפלשט"ר, ואדום הוא, ונתעסקה בו. אלמא קילור דומה לדם נדות, ואע"ג דלא הוי סומק כולי האי, וקשיא לכולהו דדייקי בין דם בחור לדם נשוי משום דסומק טפי, ובין דם מאכולת של ראש לשאר דם מאכולת:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:1:1.english: To an eye salve - [An] emplastre [a plaster], and it is red, and she had handled it. Evidently, an eye salve resembles menstrual blood, even though it is not all that red, and [this] poses a difficulty to all those who distinguish between the blood of an unmarried man and the blood of a married man because it is redder, and between the blood of a head louse and the blood of other lice.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:20:1.english: Hold the middle row - To examine the blood against it.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:20:2.hebrew: וטרפא מציעא - דההוא משובח לבדוק מכולן, ומיהו כוליה דרא כשרה לבדוק. והא דקתני כתחתון ולא כעליון, הכי קאמר: כשורה אמצעית, ולא כעליונה הימנה. והא דקתני כעליון ולא כתחתון: כשורה אמצעית, ולא כתחתונה הימנה, דאין כשר לבדוק אלא בדרא אמצעית. והא דתניא כתחתון וכ"ש כעליון, דמשמע דתרוייהו כשרין לבדוק אלא שהעליון משובח, לאו אדרי קאי, אלא אעלין דדרא מציעא. וה"ק: בעלה תחתון שהוא ברור, וכ"ש בעליון הימנה, דהיינו אמצעי, שהוא ברור מאד. והא דתניא כעליון וכ"ש כתחתון, הכי קאמר: כעליון - כעלה העליון, וכ"ש כתחתון - כעלה האמצעי:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:20:2.english: And the middle leaf - For that [leaf] is the best of all of them to examine [the blood] against; however, the entire row is valid to examine [against]. And that which is taught [in one baraita]: "Like the lower [one], and not like the upper [one]" — this is what it means: Like the middle row, and not like the one above it. And that which is taught [in another baraita]: "Like the upper [one], and not like the lower [one]" — [this means:] Like the middle row, and not like the one below it, as it is valid to examine [blood] only against the middle row. And that which is taught [in a third baraita]: "Like the lower [one], and all the more so like the upper [one]" — which implies that both are valid to examine [against], except that the upper one is superior — does not refer to the rows, but rather to the leaves of the middle row. And this is what it means: [It is valid to examine blood] against the lower leaf, which is clear, and all the more so against the one above it, which is the middle [leaf], which is very clear. And that which is taught [in the fourth baraita]: "Like the upper [one], and all the more so like the lower [one]" — this is what it means: "Like the upper" — like the upper leaf; "and all the more so like the lower" — like the middle leaf.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:21:1.english: In their clods we learned - To examine [the blood] against them, and not after their plucking.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:23:1.hebrew: ואין שיעור למים - משום דאין שיעור לעפר - אלא יביא עפר כמו שירצה, אם רב אם מעט, ויציף על מים כעובי קליפת השום למעלה מן העפר:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:23:1.english: And there is no measure for the water - Because there is no measure for the earth — rather, one may bring earth as he wishes, whether much or little, and float water over [it] to the thickness of a garlic peel above the earth.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:23:2.english: Rather, turbid - So that the appearance of the earth enters into the water.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:23:3.english: And when he muddies them - [He muddies] the water with the earth.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:1.hebrew: לא לרמיה בידיה - לא יתן העפר אל תוך ידו ויעכור המים בעפר שבידו, אע"פ שחוזר ונותנו בכלי לאחר עכירה:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:1.english: That one should not put it into his hand - One should not put the earth into his hand and muddy the water with the earth in his hand, even though he subsequently puts it into a vessel after muddying [it].

Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:2.hebrew: אבל - אם העפר בכלי, כי עכר להו בידיה באצבע, שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:2.english: But - If the earth is in a vessel, when he muddies them with his hand, [that is,] with a finger, it is fine.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:3.hebrew: או דלמא לא לעכרינהו בידיה - כשהמים בספל, לא יעכרם באצבעו, אלא בבזך או בכלי אחר:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:24:3.english: Or perhaps he should not muddy them with his hand - When the water is in the bowl, he should not muddy it with his finger, but rather with a ladle or with another vessel.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:25:1.english: Only in a cup - [A cup] of glass. Evidently, one should not put earth into water in the palm of his hand and examine [it].

Rashi on Niddah 20a:26:1.hebrew: אמר להו במקומה שנינו - שאין האדמה דומה לדם אלא במקומה, אבל הביאה במקום אחר, נשתנה מראיתה:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:26:1.english: He said to them: In its place we learned - For the earth resembles blood only in its place, but if one brought it to another place, its appearance changes.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:26:4.english: Rabbi Yishmael cursed him - [His curse was directed] at another [person] who would do so, with diphtheria.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:3:1.english: A bloodletter - One who lets blood with a horn.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:3:2.english: Between this and that - Between the first and the latter.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:4:1.hebrew: חרת שאמרו דיו - כלומר, לא כשחרורית חרת הניתך במים, אלא שחרורית חרת הניתך בדיו:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:4:1.english: The ḥeret of which they spoke is ink - That is to say, not like the blackness of ḥeret dissolved in water, but rather the blackness of ḥeret dissolved in ink.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:4:2.hebrew: כי פכחותא דדיותא - קלישות הדיו. כשהכלי מלא, יורד שחרורית החרת למטה, ומלמעלה הוא ברור ואינו שחור כל כך:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:4:2.english: Like the dilution of the ink - The thinness of the ink. When the vessel is full, the blackness of the *cheret* descends to the bottom, and from above it is clear and is not so black.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:5:1.english: In moist - In moist ink, as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:5:2.hebrew: או ביבשתא - שכן דרך שנותנין חרת בדיו כששולקים קליפות הקוצרים, והוא מתייבש:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:5:2.english: Or in dry [ink] - For such is the practice, that they put ḥeret into ink when boiling the peels or husks of harvested crops, and it dries.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:5:3.english: He would break a piece of ink - [He would] split pieces of dry ink.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:5:4.english: And he examines with it - The appearance of black blood.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:6:2.english: Like a grape - Black grapes. Another explanation: Kir is the name of a black herb.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:7:1.hebrew: עולא - אשחור דמתניתין קאי, דקתני טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:7:1.english: Ulla - Is referring to the black [blood] of the mishna, which teaches [that it is] impure.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:7:2.hebrew: סיואה - שם מקום, ועושין שם מלבושים שחורים:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:7:2.english: Siva'a - The name of a place, and they make black garments there.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:8:1.hebrew: אוליירין - בלנים, מחממי מרחצאות. לשון אחר: שם מקום:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:8:1.english: Olyarin - Bath attendants, who heat the bathhouses. Another explanation: The name of a place.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:8:2.hebrew: שמא אזכה - לגן עדן, והצדיקים מלובשים לבנים:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:8:2.english: Perhaps I will merit - [To enter] the Garden of Eden, and the righteous are dressed in white.

Rashi on Niddah 20a:9:1.hebrew: גלימי אוליירין הוו סומקי, אבל פתורי, כגון מפה וסדין, אוליירין הוו שחורין:
Rashi on Niddah 20a:9:1.english: The cloaks of the bath attendants were red, but table coverings, such as a tablecloth and a sheet, of the bath attendants were black.

Tosafot on Niddah 20a:5:1.hebrew: פלי קורטא דדיותא - מכאן משמע שדיו שלנו הוא קרוי דיו, מדקאמר קורטא דדיותא, משמע שהוא יבש. ואוסר ר"ת לכתוב ס"ת בדיו של עפצים, לפי שהוא לעולם לח. ובפ' [שני] דגיטין (דף יט.) מפורש:
Tosafot on Niddah 20a:5:1.english: [He would] break off a piece of ink - From here it is implied that our ink is that which is called "ink" (deyo), for since it states "a piece of ink" (kurta dediyuta), this implies that it is dry. And Rabbeinu Tam forbids writing a Torah scroll (sefer Torah) with gallnut ink, because it is always liquid. And in the [second] chapter of Gittin (19a), it is explained.
